items.note: Mallu Khan retook all territory between the Narbada and Bhilsa in 1536 and crowned himself at Mandu.
After Baz Bahadur's fall Malwa ceased to be independent and became a Mughal province under a governor.
Maratha incursions into Malwa intensified in 1728-1740; Mughal governor Girdhar Bahadur routed near Mandu in 1728.
Scindia and Holkar carved out principalities covering Madhya Bharat as Peshwa agents; Gwalior, Indore, Dhar and Dewas States owe their origin to this system.
In 1818 the power of the Peshwas was finally ended by the British.
A Vaishnava temple possibly existed at Besnagar in front of which the Greek ambassador erected the Garudadhvaja; nothing survives of earliest Hindu sanctuaries.
In the 7th-9th centuries temple architecture takes definite shape: the flat-roofed shrine is adorned with a tapering ornate shikhara and richer porches and door-frames.
By the 10th-12th centuries technical literature on Vastushastra had come into being to guide architects and craftsmen.
Mature temple plan: garbhagriha under a carved ceiling with lofty shikhara, and in front a large pillared Sabhamandapa for the congregation.
Nine-tenths of Madhya Bharat's ancient temples belong to the 10th-12th century wave of temple building; Udaypur named among the best.
The Udayeshwar temple stands supreme among these; it escaped the idol breakers; its crowning beauty lies in its well proportioned Shikhara and delicately carved medallions.
Alleged episode in which Muslim rulers hesitated to destroy beautiful works of art, owing to which the Udaypur temple is said to have survived.

items.note: Islamic architecture in Madhya Bharat begins in the 14th-15th century with mosques at Dhar, Mandu, Bhonrasa and Bhilsa, often converted from older Hindu temples.
No ancient palaces or residential buildings survive in Madhya Bharat; they are thought to have been built of perishable material such as wood.
Besnagar yielded three similar Yakshini figures and a Kubera figure recovered from the Betwa, free-standing colossal statues of disputed date (pre-Mauryan to Shunga).
Besnagar yielded a little under a dozen free-standing statues of the Seven Mothers, Durga, Nrisimha, Kubera, a link between earlier art and Gupta classic art.
Medieval temple architecture demanded vast numbers of figure sculptures and motifs; animal forms became highly stylised and Kirttimukha motifs bewildering.
Temples still standing at Udaipur (Udaypur) and elsewhere testify to this; images from the temples at Udaypur among others compare favourably with similar works elsewhere in India.

items.note: 1,783 monuments on the State Archaeology Department list, of which 145 declared of national importance under the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act.
Bhilsa district table row: 142 monuments in 26 places; Udaypur listed among places of important or national monuments.
Bhilsa district called the richest in Madhya Bharat for its monuments; Udaypur named among its well-known places.
Northern Madhya Bharat richest in monuments, explained by ready availability of sandstone from its hills.
Chronological table of monuments: 243 monuments in A.D. 711-1206 and 437 from 1526; Udaypur listed among places of important monuments in both periods.
Bhilsa the richest district in antiquity and historical importance; its monuments centred round ancient Vidisha at Besnagar and Udaygiri.
In 1206-1526 Islam's impact is reflected in Muslim monuments at Chanderi, Basoda, Udaypur and Bhilsa.
